title: Homotopy colimit of truncations
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and $\mathcal G^\bullet$ a cochain complex of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. The canonical map from the homotopy colimit of the good truncations $\operatorname{hocolim}_{N\to+\infty}\tau_{\le N}\mathcal G^\bullet$ to $\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. Moreover, a filtered colimit of quasi-isomorphisms of complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 06YS (successive truncations and filtered colimits in the K-flat resolution construction)

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-complex-hocolim-colimit] to the sequence of good truncations $\tau_{\le N}\mathcal G^\bullet$ with its canonical transition maps. It gives a quasi-isomorphism from $\operatorname{hocolim}_{N}\tau_{\le N}\mathcal G^\bullet$ to the termwise filtered colimit $\varinjlim_N\tau_{\le N}\mathcal G^\bullet$.

In each degree $i$, the good truncation $(\tau_{\le N}\mathcal G^\bullet)^i$ equals $\mathcal G^i$ for every $N\ge i+1$ (for $N=i$ it is $\ker d^i$, and for $N<i$ it is $0$), and the transition maps between these terms are then identities; so in each degree the sequence is eventually constant equal to $\mathcal G^i$ and the colimit in degree $i$ is $\mathcal G^i$. Thus the canonical map $\varinjlim_N\tau_{\le N}\mathcal G^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ is an isomorphism of cochain complexes, hence a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. Composing with Step 1 proves the truncation assertion.

Let $(f_j:E_j^\bullet\to F_j^\bullet)_{j\in J}$ be a filtered diagram of quasi-isomorphisms. For $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ to be abelian the site is small, or essentially so [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; replacing $\mathcal C$ by an equivalent small site does not change $\Mod(\mathcal O)$, so the hypothesis of [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] holds and by it filtered colimits in the sheaf-of-$\mathcal O$-modules category are exact. Therefore kernels, images, and cohomology of the termwise colimit commute with the filtered colimit, so $H^i(\varinjlim_jE_j^\bullet)\cong\varinjlim_jH^i(E_j^\bullet)$ and likewise for $F_j^\bullet$. The induced map on these groups is the filtered colimit of the isomorphisms $H^i(f_j)$, hence is an isomorphism for every $i$; the induced map of colimit complexes is a quasi-isomorphism.

tool_uses.why: Its statement supplies exact filtered colimits in the module category on an arbitrary ringed site, needed to commute filtered colimits with kernels and images.
